definition.name: Cut the Loss — the world's tactical calculus
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: When Morpheus is captured, every institutional logic converges on the same near-certain answer: he is a spent asset, so preserve what remains and abandon him. Smith reads the doubled serum driving Morpheus's mind into an ordered wave as the sign the key is about to break (ev-031), the crew's own survival protocol is to pull Morpheus's plug rather than mount a rescue (ev-032), and once the ship is hunted Morpheus himself converts instantly to preservation — reading the Sentinels, buying minutes, ordering the EMP (ev-040). The situation makes self-preservation the rational move and frames any rescue as an irrational gamble against overwhelming odds.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the world's 'impossible-odds' texture is laid down here — Smith corrects the Lieutenant's belief that the raid is succeeding by reporting his own two units already dead, treating the outcome as a foregone calculus. This is the Cut-the-Loss world's baseline premise: force is overwhelming and得失
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: No earlier member; this is the plot's opening premise — the Agents as a near-certain, self-replenishing force against which any rescue reads as an irrational gamble.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the agents' coordinated, converging split models the world's systematic hunting logic — the same institutional pressure that later renders Morpheus a spent asset and any rescue an irrational gamble.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-001: Because the raid is already a foregone calculus (ev-001), the hunt can be executed as a clean division of labor — Brown inside, Smith to the alley — i.e. pressure applied as procedure rather than desperation.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Trinity survives by outrunning a closing, near-certain trap (matching leap, racing the truck), dramatizing the 'overwhelming odds' premise that the Cut-the-Loss logic will later invoke to argue rescue is irrational.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-002: The converging approaches set in ev-002 are what force Trinity upward and across the rooftops; her narrow escape is the world proving its own premise that survival requires outrunning, not out-fighting, the system.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Smith's bargain — wipe Neo's record in exchange for Morpheus — is the world offering the rational self-preservation trade (betray the asset to save yourself); Neo's contemptuous refusal is the first personal rejection of the calculus the plot tracks.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-003: Trinity's escape (ev-003) closes one hunt and redirects institutional pressure onto the next available asset, Neo; the interrogation is the system re-applying its cost-benefit logic to a captured operator.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the extraction of the implanted tracker materializes the system's totalizing grip and the cost of being marked — the institutional pressure that makes flight, not fight, the rational move.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-007: The bug Smith animates into Neo in ev-007 is the very object Trinity must later cut out; its removal is the crew paying the price of the system's mark so they can return to evasion.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Neo recoils from the crew 'as agents of an unbearable violation,' reading liberation through the system's own terms — the world's framing of self-preservation (stay plugged, stay safe) as the sane choice.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-009: Once the tracker is out (ev-009) Neo is physically free yet still thinks in the Matrix's vocabulary; the Desert of the Real is where that internalized calculus — liberation as threat — surfaces.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the Sentinel hunt forces the ship to kill power, arm the EMP, and lie 'cold and silent' — pure self-preservation through hiding. It establishes the survival-protocol logic the plot will later see Morpheus himself enforce.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-013: Neo's induction into the truth of the real world (ev-013) places him aboard the ship just before its first real-world hunt; the Sentinel sweep is the consequence of being a marked ship in a machine-patrolled world.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the trap closes as the Matrix is rewritten, Mouse is killed, and the crew is sealed in — the world's overwhelming force reasserting impossible odds. Morpheus's desperate seizure of a traceable phone is the first move that will expose and lose him.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-019: The ship's hiding protocol in ev-019 buys the crew's survival but does not end the hunt; the same machine pressure that drove them to ground re-manifests inside the Matrix as a rewritten building and a closing trap.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the crew hides inside a wall and worms down stack pipes to escape a floor-by-floor sweep — collective self-preservation through concealment under overwhelming pressure, the survival logic that will later make rescue look reckless.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-023: Morpheus's traceable-phone gambit in ev-023 exposes their position, so the only rational response is concealment and withdrawal — hiding in the wet-wall rather than fighting the sweep.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Morpheus is buried under 'a rush of cops' and seized by 'a wall of cops' while Tank cries out — the capture that makes him, in the plot's terms, a spent asset and turns the rescue into an irrational gamble.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-024: The concealment-and-retreat logic of ev-024 funnels the crew toward the basement exit; it is there, covering the descent, that Morpheus is overwhelmed — the survival protocol failing to save the one who stays to fight.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: the crew regroups to learn Morpheus is 'alive but being moved to an unknown location' while Cypher is already at an exit — the divergent positions (captured asset vs. self-preserving deserter) that set up the plot's central arithmetic.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-026: Morpheus's capture (ev-026) produces exactly two downstream states — a lost leader to be accounted for, and a crew that must decide whether that asset is worth recovering — which is the split ev-027 records.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Smith reads the doubled serum driving Morpheus's mind into an ordered wave as the sign the key is about to break — the world's institutional logic declaring Morpheus a spent asset whose information is about to be lost, i.e. the rational reason to cut the loss.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-027: Learning Morpheus is alive but being moved (ev-027) leads directly to the interrogation room, where the system converts a captured asset into a breaking one — the clock the crew's calculus must run against.

chain.why_in_plot: Turn: the crew's own survival protocol is to pull Morpheus's plug rather than mount a rescue — self-preservation made into procedure, framing any rescue as an irrational gamble against overwhelming odds. This is the plot's thesis stated as action.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: Smith's read that Morpheus is about to break (ev-031) tells the crew the asset is already lost; their rational response is to deny the system its prize by unplugging him — the arithmetic of loss applied to a man still breathing.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Brown reports the trace has fixed the crew's position and Jones 'orders a Sentinel strike' — institutional logic converging to eliminate the now-exposed asset — while Smith 'withdraws from the unit in disgust,' the system itself treating the rescue as a foregone, unwinnable calculus.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: Neo's decision to go back in (ev-032) triggers the rescue, whose traceable hardline exit exposes the crew's position; the Agents' Sentinel strike is the world re-applying its cost-benefit logic to close the now-open breach.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup: Trinity is ripped back to the ship and Tank refuses to send her back for Neo ('he cannot') — the survival protocol overriding loyalty, the rational abandonment of an exposed asset. Neo left 'alone in the subway' is the arithmetic of loss applied once more.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-036: The trace and Sentinel strike in ev-036 force an emergency exit under fire; with the ship hunted, Tank's refusal to risk a second operator is the same survival logic — one asset already written off, do not spend another.

chain.why_in_plot: Turn: once the ship is hunted, Morpheus himself converts instantly to preservation — reading the Sentinels on radar, buying the crew five or six minutes, and ordering Tank to charge the EMP — the spent asset now enforcing the very survival logic that had marked him for loss.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-037: Neo left behind and the ship exposed (ev-037) is exactly the hunted-ship condition that demands the cold protocol; Morpheus, freshly rescued and still a 'spent' man, is the one who now imposes it, completing the plot's argument that preservation is the rational reflex.

chain.why_in_plot: Resolution: when Neo is shot and the life monitors flatline, the crew gives him up — the arithmetic of loss applied again — against which Trinity refuses the verdict and brings the monitors back to life. The Cut-the-Loss world's answer is stated at its starkest so the plot's tension is fully spent.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-040: The EMP-and-hide protocol of ev-040 fails to keep the crew whole — Neo is lost in the fight — and the ship, once more hunted, reverts to the same calculus: when the monitors flatline they write him off, the final application of the arithmetic this plot has traced throughout.

definition.name: The Wager on a Man — Neo's refusal of the arithmetic
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Neo resolves the dilemma from the inside by refusing its logic rather than solving it: he explicitly denies he is the One, so going back carries no prophetic cover and is a pure wager on a man (ev-032). His choice is the only thing he can live with because Morpheus already gave his life for him (ev-025), making self-preservation a cost to his emerging self-respect he will not pay. The refusal to flee holds through to the end — cornered in the subway and urged to run, he turns back from the escalator to face the hunter (ev-038).

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo is drawn toward the truth 'against his plan to work the next day' — the first tug of a pull that will later become a choice made with no prophetic cover, a pure wager. It names the question the whole arc answers.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: Provides the initial state of a man already leaning toward something larger than self-preservation, which the ordinary-world reassertion (ev-005) then pushes against.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. The mundane reprimand and either-or ultimatum reassert the 'rational,' self-preserving ordinary life Neo will later refuse; the vast question he 'carries still, pushed to the background' is the seed of the wager.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-004: The night's pull (ev-004) collapses into a morning of compliance, establishing the self-preserving default whose refusal the arc will dramatize.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo is driven to a window ledge 'he cannot bring himself to cross' and climbs back inside — an early failure of nerve that the later refusal-to-flee arc (escalator turnback, ev-038) answers.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-005: The ordinary-world compliance (ev-005) leaves Neo unprepared for real danger, so when the raid comes he recoils from the ledge rather than committing — the behavioral baseline the arc will reverse.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo is tempted to bolt ('opens the door to bolt') but, reframed by Trinity, 'closes the door and stays' — the first enacted refusal of the self-preserving exit, consenting to enter a war.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-006: The ledge failure (ev-006) establishes the self-preserving reflex that this event begins to override: faced with another threshold he again hesitates, but this time stays.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo chooses 'knowing' over forgetting by swallowing the red pill — a self-risking choice of truth over comfortable self-preservation, the decisive turn toward the wager and the cost he accepts to leave the cave.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-008: Having consented to enter the war (ev-008), Neo is now positioned to make the irreversible self-risking choice that the staying opened the door to.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo is 'born into the real world' through rupture, near-drowning, and extraction — the physical price his wager incurs, grounding the later self-sacrifice cost in the body.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-010: Swallowing the red pill (ev-010) triggers the trace and extraction, so the brutal rebirth is the direct physical consequence of the choice to know.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Morpheus, 'certain they have found the one,' rebuilds Neo and begins dismantling his assumptions — the faith-in-a-man pressure acting directly on Neo's self-conception, initiating the internal shift.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-011: Only after the body is recovered and rebuilt from the rebirth (ev-011) can Morpheus set to work on Neo's mind and self-image.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo's body 'speaks' the unbearable truth — recoiling, screaming, vomiting, blacking out — the self-sacrifice horn felt physically: the price of accepting reality over comforting illusion.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-012: The dismantling of assumptions (ev-012) leads Neo up the ladder to the deck, where the truth he is being shown becomes physically unbearable and his body revolts.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo 'accepts there is no going back' and commits to be guided into training — the main-character's first conscious acceptance of the costly path, the self-sacrifice turn.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-013: Having endured the unbearable revelation (ev-013), Neo lies awake and, rather than retreat, accepts there is no going back — the conscious commitment that follows the shock.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo's breakthrough comes 'not through understanding but through rage' — he learns the world 'answers to the mind, not the muscles,' the internal override of imposed limits that the wager-on-himself will later demand.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-014: Commitment to training (ev-014) places Neo in the dojo where the download's false confidence is tested and the real lesson — mind over muscle — is forged.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Morpheus teaches that Neo 'can surpass any Agent because their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not' — the doctrine that individual will overrides the system's fixed calculus, the intellectual ground for refusing the dilemma's arithmetic.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-015: The mind-over-muscle lesson (ev-015) prepares the doctrinal step: having learned the world answers to the mind, Neo is now taught that the rules binding the system do not bind him.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Morpheus pins the Agent and orders Trinity to get Neo out, giving his own life so Neo can escape; this gift of a life is the debt that later makes self-preservation a cost to Neo's self-respect he will not pay.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-018: The training (ev-018) culminates in the field operation during which the Agents close in and Morpheus makes the sacrifice that becomes the arc's moral fulcrum.

chain.why_in_plot: Turn. Neo stops the plug from being pulled and commits to going back, explicitly denying he is the One so the mission becomes a pure wager on a man rather than a prophecy — the refusal of the dilemma's arithmetic from the inside.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-025: Morpheus's self-gift (ev-025) creates the debt that makes fleeing unbearable to Neo's self-respect; when the plug is about to be pulled, that debt is what he refuses to honor by saving only himself.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo 'leaps after' Morpheus and catches him — the wager made physical, a self-risking act against the odds that enacts the commitment he made at the plug.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: The decision to go back for a man (ev-032) launches the rescue, and the mid-dive leap to catch the falling Morpheus is the physical payoff of that wager.

chain.why_in_plot: Resolution. Cornered in the subway and urged by Trinity to run, Neo does not run — he turns back from the escalator to face the hunter, holding the refusal to flee through to the end of the arc.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-034: The rescue (ev-034) delivers the crew to the escape that funnels Neo into the subway, where, cornered and urged to run, he enacts the same refusal-to-flee the whole arc has built toward.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. At the edge of death Neo 'refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces,' summons an impossible surge, and breaks free — the internal refusal of imposed inevitability made physical, the wager-on-himself at its most extreme.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-038: Turning to face the hunter (ev-038) forces the confrontation with Smith, and that standoff is what drives Neo to the edge of death where he refuses the fate pronounced over him.

chain.why_in_plot: Setup. Neo runs a gauntlet that 'tightens at every block' — the overwhelming odds against which his refusal-to-flee (escalator turnback, ev-038) is measured, the cost of the wager made into a running report as Smith closes to point-blank.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-039: Breaking free from Smith (ev-039) does not end the threat; it sends Neo sprinting, and the gauntlet that tightens at every block is the direct pursuit that follows the subway surge.

chain.why_in_plot: Connective. Trinity refuses to accept Neo's death, taking hold of his body, kissing him, and bringing the monitors back to life against the crew's verdict — the bond's loyalty overriding survival and carrying the wager forward when Neo's own refusal has cost him his life.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-041: The gauntlet (ev-041) ends with Neo cornered and shot — Smith's settled verdict — which produces the death the crew accepts and Trinity then refuses, so the flight's fatal outcome is what her loyalty overrides.

definition.name: Faith Made Flesh — Morpheus as the living argument for sacrifice
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Morpheus is the embodied case for the sacrifice horn, having already given his life so Neo and Trinity escape (ev-025) and, while captured and drugged, spending his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking rather than saving himself by betraying the crew (ev-031). His faith then reframes Neo's illogical gamble as destiny — reinterpreting both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation of the One (ev-035) — pressing Neo toward the belief that a man is worth any risk and converting a faith-wager back into purpose.

It plants the stance that a man is worth betting on before a.

definition.name: Loyalty Over Survival — the Neo–Trinity bond
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: In the Neo–Trinity bond the dilemma is felt as loyalty versus survival, and their 'we' becomes the force that overrides the world's cut-the-loss logic. Gutted by both Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial, Trinity converts grief into command and makes the rescue possible only on her terms (ev-032); the bond runs on protective reciprocity even in escape, as Neo breaks free of her embrace to send her out first (ev-030). It culminates in her refusing to accept Neo's death at all — taking hold of his body, kissing him, and bringing the monitors back to life against the crew's verdict (ev-044).

definition.name: A Community Pricing a Life — the crew's split
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: The crew collectively lives out both horns of the dilemma. Cypher carries self-preservation to its logical end — first recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a mere body count to retreat Neo toward caution (ev-020), then murdering Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents to save himself, only to be struck down by the surviving Tank (ev-029). The rest of the crew — Tank, Switch, Apoc, Dozer — pay the price of the sacrifice horn, and their split between doubters and believers during Neo's failed jump shows a community wrestling with whether any one man is worth dying for (ev-016).

chain.why_in_plot: The crew watches Neo's failed jump split between doubters and believers — the community openly wrestling with whether any one man is worth dying for, before a single betrayal has occurred.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: OPENING establishes the crew as the unit that will price a life; the jump is the first moment the community visibly divides over whether their leader's faith is worth the risk.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a mere body count to push Neo toward caution — the community's first voice arguing that no leader is worth dying for.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-016: The jump's public split between doubters and believers licenses Cypher to voice the doubter's arithmetic aloud, translating the silent hesitation on the deck into an explicit body-count argument.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can — the first concrete act of betrayal, carrying self-preservation toward its logical end and seeding the crew's split.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-020: Having reframed the prophecy as a body count he is unwilling to pay, Cypher converts that calculation into action, planting the hidden line that will later summon the crew into the trap.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher reaches the exit, draws a concealed rifle, and the others crawl toward the ringing phone — the split made lethal, self-preservation now armed against the community.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-021: The covertly planted phone is the same line that now rings to draw the crew back; Cypher's early act of wiring a secret exit matures into him reaching that exit first, weapon in hand, while the others answer the ring he set up.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher carries self-preservation to its logical end — murdering Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents — the community's price-calculation turned into actual bodies.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-028: Reaching the exit and drawing the concealed rifle puts Cypher physically ahead of and armed against the crew, enabling him to shoot Tank, lie to Trinity, and kill Apoc and Switch as they jack back in defenseless.

chain.why_in_plot: The surviving crew pays the sacrifice horn's price — Trinity wakes to Dozer's death and reads Tank's face for more loss — the community left to absorb the cost of Cypher's betrayal.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-029: Cypher's murders of Dozer (via the lightning strike) and of Apoc and Switch, and his near-killing of Tank, leave exactly the survivors who wake to count the dead, so the community is forced to take the betrayal's cost into its arms.
